strategy: Change performance authoring before another six-second parameter-tuning pass. Retain the native rig, IK, contact checks and independent character routes as infrastructure.

method.media: Independently fully decoded both delivered six-second movies, 144 frames each at 24 fps; native and both movie hashes match final handoff.
method.visual_review: Viewed all 144 close and all 144 shot-size frames in chronological decoded contact sheets. Also viewed contact sheets of 16 independently extracted actual full-frame samples from each movie.
method.limitation: No continuous or full-speed playback. Previous supported CUA initialization failed twice with: trusted Node process exited unexpectedly; kernel reset, rerun your request. Frame-based timing judgments are provisional pending normal-speed viewing.
method.mutations: No production/source edits, integration, native rendering or messages to production. Only local review artifacts written in the task workspace.

improvements_over_v011.observation: The heel kick against the small obstacle makes the toe snag more intelligible in the close framing. It remains a small, brief cue in the shot-size framing.
improvements_over_v011.qualification: The measured pinned-toe and continued-root-motion claims are in the supplied technical evidence; they do not independently prove persuasive weight.

improvements_over_v011.observation: Earlier catch heel and subsequent compression remove the v011 pre-landing rise/double bob. The descent is cleaner.
The girl's early brake/compression is now separated from the boy's compression, removing the conspicuous paired catch response.
Short neck and ankle connectors remove distracting proxy gaps. Missing paint is not the main remaining limitation.

remaining_artistic_failures.observation: The girl's waiting pose resembles a held extended mid-step/lunge: front support planted, trailing heel raised, with nearly unchanged body line, head and arms. Independent timing does not yet create a clear choice to wait or attend to the boy.

The boy's recovery is still a smooth prescribed rise. The sequence has little distinct shoulder, head and hip counter-action to explain effort and balance. This is broader than the old rigid torso hinge, which has improved.

The later walk remains upright, regular and pendular, with restrained arm and torso response. Small phase lags and root modulation do not fundamentally change the performance. No obvious large stance-foot slide was apparent in the inspected frames; that does not validate force or calibrated center-of-mass behavior.

recommended_next_work: Do not transplant painted character assets or integrate v012 into the trailer yet.

Use observed movement reference to author a short whole-pose trip/catch/recovery study. Establish force direction, support changes, torso/head counter-action and distinct reacting/waiting behavior before smoothing curves.

Review the blocked study continuously at normal speed and at intended shot size before polishing, extending the walk or repainting. Keep the existing contact checks as constraints rather than the primary generator of performance.

An isolated next iteration is useful if it changes this authoring method. Another full six-second pass of small procedural timing/offset adjustments is unlikely to resolve the central weakness. A change of software is not required.

preview_delivery.note: Existing successful specialist upload; no new upload performed during this review.
